summary: A best current practice describing how IRTF research groups are formed and run, and how their participants relate to the IRSG and the IAB. It covers the procedures, not any technical protocol.

eli5.summary: It is the rulebook for starting and running a science club. It says how to form the club and who the club reports to.

questions: how are irtf research groups formed
what is in an irtf research group charter
how does the irtf differ from the ietf
subtitle: How IRTF research groups are formed, run and closed, and who does what.

tldr.problem: The IRTF needed a shared description of how its long-term research groups are chartered, run and ended, and how they relate to the IRSG and the IAB.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC sets out a five-part charter reviewed by the IRSG and approved by the IAB, light operating guidelines, a termination path, and duties for each role.
tldr.outcome: It gives research groups wide freedom: no consensus requirement, optional limited membership, and success judged by research quality and impact.

today: RFC 2014 is a Best Current Practice and its metadata shows no obsoleting or updating RFC. It describes IRTF procedures as of October 1996 and is based on RFC 1603.

sections.title: The IRTF and Its Research Groups
sections.content:
The Internet Research Task Force (IRTF) focuses on longer term research issues, while the IETF focuses on shorter term engineering and standards. The IRTF is made of a number of focused, long-term, small Research Groups with stable membership. Participation is by individual contributors, not representatives of organizations.

The IRTF Chair manages the IRTF in consultation with the Internet Research Steering Group (IRSG). The IRSG includes the IRTF Chair, the Research Group chairs and possibly members at large. The IAB appoints the IRTF Chair, and IRSG members at large are chosen by the IRTF Chair with IRSG consultation and IAB approval.

The IRTF does not set standards. Research Group output may be journal papers, white papers or Informational RFCs, and technology may be brought to the IETF. Group input carries no more weight than other community input and goes through the same standards process. Unlike IETF Working Groups, which are always open, Research Groups may have open or closed membership, so they must report progress regularly and are encouraged to hold occasional open meetings.
sections.eli5: The IETF builds the rules for today, while the IRTF is a set of small clubs that study questions for later. A club may be invite-only, but it has to tell everyone what it learns.

sections.title: Forming a Research Group
sections.content:
A group may start at the initiative of an individual or a set of individuals. They submit a charter and a list of proposed founding members to the IRTF Chair. The IRSG reviews the charter and forwards it to the IAB for approval. If approved, the charter is placed on the IRTF Web site and published in the Internet Monthly Report.

The IRTF Chair, IRSG and IAB consider whether the research area is clear and relevant, whether the group will foster work that would not otherwise be done, whether it overlaps with another group, and whether there is enough interest and expertise. The RFC says at least four or five active participants are typically required, since one person cannot handle management, editing and writing. The IAB also checks how the work relates to the architecture of the Internet Protocol Suite.
sections.eli5: To start a club, you write down what it is for and who will join. Some grown-ups check that the idea is clear, useful and does not copy another club.

sections.title: The Five-Part Charter
sections.content:
A charter is a contract between a Research Group and the IRTF to conduct research in the designated area, and it may be renegotiated periodically. It has five sections:

  • Name: descriptive, with an acronym of at most 8 printable ASCII characters that does not conflict with IETF names.
  • Chair(s): one or two, with email addresses.
  • Mailing list(s): a contact address and an open interest list, with subscription procedures and archive location. A members-only list is also expected.
  • Membership policy: open or limited, and how to apply. Limited membership is permitted but not encouraged or required.
  • Description: the focus and intent, with a first paragraph summarizing the area, goals and approach, plus objectives and expected impact on the Internet architecture.
sections.eli5: The club's sign-up sheet has five parts: its name, its leaders, how to contact it, who may join, and what it is trying to find out.

sections.title: How Groups Operate and Meet
sections.content:
Research Groups are autonomous and decide most operating details themselves. Because their products are research results rather than standards, consensus of the group is not required. Success is measured by the quality and impact of the results.

For structured meetings the Chair must publish a draft agenda to the group mailing list well in advance, with the items, the estimated time per item, and the documents to read first. Meetings may be by telephone, video or face to face. Written minutes are strongly encouraged, with the agenda, the high points and the attendees. Face-to-face meetings are encouraged to be co-located with IETF meetings. Meeting documents should be available at least two weeks before the meeting.
sections.eli5: Each club mostly runs itself. Before a meeting the leader sends out a plan, and afterward someone writes down what was said so absent members can catch up.

sections.title: Ending a Group and the Roles Involved
sections.content:
If a group is not making progress on its chartered areas, or does not regularly report its results, the IRTF Chair can, in consultation with the group, require a recharter, request new Chair(s), or disband the group. The group may appeal to the IAB if it disagrees.

The IRTF Chair plans, coordinates groups, reports to the IAB and the community, and tracks progress through regular status reports. IRSG members advise on chartering new groups. The Research Group Chair manages process and content, moderates the email list, organizes meetings, makes sure minutes are taken, spreads the work and works with the RFC Editor on publication. Taking minutes and editing is often done by a designated Editor or Secretary.
sections.eli5: If a club stops doing anything or stops sharing, the head of the clubs can ask it to change its goals, pick new leaders, or close. The club can ask a higher group to take another look.

sections.title: Documents and RFC Publication
sections.content:
Group work usually results in research papers and Informational or Experimental RFCs. A document can be written by an individual in the group, by the group with a designated Editor, or by others, and the authors need not include the Chair. Authorship by the entire group is not required.

The RFC notes that the RFC series is a publication mechanism only and publication does not determine status: all Internet Standards are published as RFCs, but not all RFCs specify standards. Experimental publication generally requires IESG review, and initial publication as an Internet Draft is preferred. The memo says security issues are not discussed.
sections.eli5: When a club writes something up, it can be printed in the big public library of notes. Being printed there does not mean the idea is an official rule.

references.text: Internet Architecture Board and Internet Engineering Steering Group, "The Internet Standards Process -- Revision 2", RFC 1602, March 1994.
